name: Hidden Couloir
approach: From the Stuart Lake trailhead (3,400 ft), hike the Stuart Lake Trail then Colchuck Lake Trail about 4 miles to Colchuck Lake (5,570 ft). Traverse the lake's south/east shore and ascend talus to the base of the Hidden Couloir at roughly 6,400 ft, just east of the lowest point of Dragontail's north face.

waypoints.name: Stuart Lake Trailhead
waypoints.note: Self-issue day-use wilderness permit and NW Forest Pass required at the kiosk; parking fills fast in this heavily-trafficked Enchantments quota area.
waypoints.directions: The Stuart Lake Trailhead sits at about 3,400 ft at the end of FR-7601, off Icicle Creek Road. A Northwest Forest Pass and a self-issue day-use wilderness permit are both required at the kiosk. This is the main trailhead for the heavily-trafficked Enchantments quota area and the parking fills fast, so arrive early.

waypoints.name: Colchuck Lake / Stuart Lake trail split
waypoints.note: Signed junction roughly 2-2.5 mi in; bear left onto Colchuck Lake Trail #1599A.

waypoints.name: Colchuck Lake
waypoints.note: Established backcountry camps and reliable water near the outlet; dogs prohibited in the Enchantment Permit Area.

waypoints.name: Lateral moraine crest (Colchuck Glacier)
waypoints.note: Boulder-hop the south/east shore then gain the moraine crest deposited by the Colchuck Glacier to avoid loose talus below the north face.

waypoints.name: Hidden Couloir base
waypoints.note: Base of the north-face couloir system below the glacier's east lobe; check avalanche and icefall conditions before committing in winter/spring.

waypoints.name: Mid-face ice runnels
waypoints.note: Route narrows through runnels splitting the mid-face rock band; reported as thin, unpredictable ice depending on the season.

waypoints.name: Dragontail Peak summit
waypoints.note: True summit; descend the standard Aasgard Pass scramble route back to Colchuck Lake.
